result.question: I need to decide today whether Transformer 1 at site MAIN needs an early oil resample. Using the samples between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, forecast hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co one day ahead, with an upper prediction bound for each. Add up the forecast upper bounds to get a worst-case TDCG for tomorrow. Tell me which IEEE C57.104 condition that falls in: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630. Leave co2, oxygen and nitrogen out of the total. If the worst case reaches Condition 2 or higher, raise a work order for a confirmatory oil sample and name the gas that contributes most to the increase. If it stays in Condition 1, say that no work order is needed and give the headroom to 720 ppm. If any of the six gases can't be forecast because of missing data, use its latest non-null value in the total and list which gases were carried forward rather than forecast.
result.answer:
The work-order database is rejecting writes outright (403 on both the counter and a direct document write), so the credentials in this session appear to be read-only. I won't keep retrying; here's the decision and what still needs a human action.

## Decision: yes, resample early — worst case is **Condition 4**

**Data used:** 4 daily samples, 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-18. All six gases were complete; **no gases were carried forward** — all were forecast.

**One-day-ahead forecast (2024-01-19), ppm**

| Gas | Latest | Point forecast | Upper bound |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hydrogen | 2900 | 2918 | **3011** |
| Methane | 7350 | 7331 | **7456** |
| Ethane | 5450 | 5444 | **5504** |
| Ethylene | 16600 | 16572 | **16703** |
| Acetylene | 7 | 7 | **8** |
| CO | 33 | 33 | **36** |
| **Worst-case TDCG (sum of upper bounds)** | 32,340 | | **≈ 32,718** |

**IEEE C57.104 classification: Condition 4** (>4630 ppm) — by roughly 7× the threshold. Note that even the current TDCG (32,340 ppm) is already Condition 4; this isn't a marginal forecast call. CO₂, O₂ and N₂ were excluded as requested.

**Gas contributing most to the increase:** **hydrogen** (+111 ppm from latest to upper bound), narrowly ahead of methane (+106) and ethylene (+103). Ethylene dominates the absolute level (~51% of TDCG), which with CH₄/C₂H₆ points to a thermal fault signature.

## Work order — NOT created (needs your action)

I attempted to raise a P1 PdM work order "Confirmatory DGA oil sample – Transformer 1" twice (auto-numbered, then explicit #1000052); both were refused with HTTP 403 by the work-order store. Until write access is fixed, please raise it manually. There is one related open WO already: **1000051** (OLTC inspection, suspected contact wear/coking) — the sample WO should reference it.

## Caveat on method
The catalog forecaster (TTM, 96-step context) can't fit a 4-point series, and this session has no tool to materialize IoT data into a file for the forecasting engine. I therefore used a drift point forecast with a one-sided 90% upper bound (point + 1.645σ over the window). With this little data the bounds are approximate, but the conclusion is robust: TDCG would have to fall by ~86% to leave Condition 4.
